quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. What do they indicate?

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: How does improper braking affect motorcycle safety?

options.text: Usually has no consequences.
Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
Should not be a concern, since the motorcycle has two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Using the correct braking technique is essential for safe riding.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle fit you?

options.text: Your fingertips should barely reach the handlebars when you are seated on the motorcycle.
The seat should be one foot higher than your waist when you are standing next to the motorcycle.
Your feet should comfortably reach the ground when you are seated on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet should comfortably reach the ground when you are seated on the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you correctly if your feet comfortably touch the ground while you are sitting on it. Always check that a motorcycle fits before you ride it.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue while riding?

options.text: Turn on the radio.
Take frequent rest breaks.
Drink caffeine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent rest breaks.
questions.explanation: Take frequent rest breaks during long rides to reduce fatigue. Caffeine can make fatigue worse when it wears off. Bad weather also increases fatigue, so dress warmly and use a windshield for long rides.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle begins moving again.
Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, move to a different lane to give it space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of?

options.text: Leather.
Wool.
Any soft material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or a similar durable material for the best grip and protection.

questions.question: How should your helmet fit for maximum protection?

options.text: Fits snugly.
Is clean.
Looks cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Your helmet will protect you best if it meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no damage.

questions.question: How can other motorists see you more easily while riding?

options.text: Wear brightly-colored clothing while riding.
Wear darkly-colored clothing while riding.
Wave your arms while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear brightly-colored clothing while riding.
questions.explanation: Wear brightly-colored clothing to make it easier for others to see you. This helps at any time of day.

questions.question: What should you do if a tailgater is following you?

options.text: Allow them to pass.
Speed up.
Not change how you are riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow them to pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. Speeding up will just make them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Let them pass by slowing down or changing lanes.
Speed up to create distance between you and the tailgater.
Ignore the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass by slowing down or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: If you can do so safely, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may only cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, which increases danger.

questions.question: When riding, your boots or shoes should:

options.text: Cover your ankles.
Have long heels.
Have long and loose laces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Your footwear should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they won't catch on surfaces. Shoelaces should be tucked in so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Which material provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Fleece
Leather
Denim

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather or sturdy synthetic materials provide the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, their effects:

options.text: Are less dangerous than when either is used alone.
Often balance each other out.
Can be stronger than when either is used alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can impair your riding ability. Some medications become more dangerous when combined with alcohol.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Accidentally move into another lane of traffic.
Get through the turn faster.
Keep control of their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accidentally move into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause you to cross into another lane of traffic or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: Having one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: Will not result in a DUI conviction.
Will never affect your riding skills.
Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Your ability to ride safely is affected starting with your first drink. You can be convicted of impaired riding even if you are below the legal blood alcohol limit.

questions.question: Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle for the first time, you should:

options.text: Just start riding. Learning by doing is the best way.
Just start riding. Most bikes are similar, so you don't need to learn its safety features.
Practice with the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how the bike operates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice with the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how the bike operates.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar bike, check its safety and maintenance. Find where everything is located. Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how it works.

questions.question: An ideal lane position should:

options.text: Help you see others and be seen.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: It affects your steering, which affects your balance.
It will disable your front brake.
It will prevent you from accelerating.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects your steering, which affects your balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because it interferes with your steering, which is essential for balance. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: When being followed by a tailgater, you should:

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more space ahead.
Ignore them.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more space ahead.
questions.explanation: If a tailgater is following you, ride in a way that encourages them to pass. Riding faster may only cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, increasing danger.

questions.question: When choosing a jacket for protection, it should:

options.text: Fit loosely and flap in the wind.
Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Not be made of leather or another sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material. They should fit snugly enough to not flap in the wind, but loosely enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT recommended as protective gear for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Long pants
Gloves
A baseball cap

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap
questions.explanation: Wear protective gear when riding. Good options include long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, closed-toe boots that cover your ankles, and full-fingered leather gloves. Cover as much skin as possible.

questions.question: A sign that your rear tire has gone flat is:

options.text: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
You hear a loud noise.
You see air coming out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire goes flat, the back of your motorcycle may jerk or sway from side to side. If this happens, stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes since it is light outside.
Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you better.
Wear shorts if it is hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright clothes when riding to make yourself visible to other drivers, even in daylight.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may proceed through the intersection with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in the direction you want to go.
